paragraphs.text: Until recently, tall buildings were made almost entirely of steel and concrete. A material called cross-laminated timber is changing this. It is made by gluing layers of wood together, with the grain of each layer at right angles to the one below, which makes the panels extremely strong.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The tallest wooden building completed so far stands 85 metres high and contains apartments, a hotel and offices. Its builders say that the wooden panels were manufactured in a factory and assembled on site, which reduced construction time by around a quarter.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The main concern about wooden buildings is fire. Tests have shown, however, that thick timber panels burn slowly: the outer layer turns to charcoal, which protects the wood inside. Most regulations still limit the height of wooden buildings, but several countries are reviewing their rules.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Wood also has environmental advantages. Trees absorb carbon dioxide as they grow, and the carbon remains stored in the timber for as long as the building stands. Producing steel and concrete, by contrast, releases large amounts of the gas.
paragraphs.label: D
